scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a 590-610/month Jun-Jul baseline to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07).
Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (E-01); the majority sit on ACTUAL reads.
Field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep, covering 9200 accounts (E-02).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Since August 2026, field manual-read route completion for the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts (E-02); the resulting incomplete/late reads trigger estimate substitution at billing import, producing ESTIMATED-read bills that account for part of the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-01, E-07). Dispute response handling remains within SLA (E-03), so this field-read-coverage degradation — not slow ticket handling — is the best-supported mechanism, though it explains only the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240/3025) of disputed bills, leaving the ACTUAL-read majority (1785/3025) unexplained by current evidence.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/throughput problem (slow manual ticket handling), not a fundamental billing-accuracy defect, so automating ticket answers would address it.

H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused more reads to be rejected or mis-substituted with estimates, producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-PIPELINE-FAILURE.statement: A degradation in the AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) caused missing or late register reads, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-QUALITY.statement: Degraded manual meter-read completion or accuracy by the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) since August led to more estimated/incorrect bills.

H-BILLING-CALC-ERROR.statement: Billing/tariff calculation defects applied to bills with accepted ACTUAL reads (independent of read-source failure) drive the larger share of disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (E-01): the majority of disputes sit on bills billed from ACTUAL reads, not estimates. This means estimate-substitution theories (AMI export failure, import rule rejection) can at best explain the smaller ESTIMATED share and leave the larger ACTUAL-read dispute volume unaccounted for.

Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 is 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts (E-02). This shows a measurable shortfall in manual read coverage during the dispute-surge window, consistent with a field-service degradation feeding incorrect/estimated bills, but the record alone does not say how many of those shortfall accounts actually became disputed bills.

E-02 still shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 — that measurement stands. It no longer supports the premise that this shortfall produced the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, since E-12 shows those bills' underlying meters are AMI (95.5% rejected-at-import, 4.5% no-read), not the manual field-read population E-02 measures.

crm-tickets dispute_response_times (E-03) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets: response handling is currently within SLA, not slow. This undercuts the premise that slow manual ticket handling is driving the dispute surge, since turnaround times look acceptable rather than degraded.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned 0 records (E-04): no tariff changes are logged for the window examined. This rules out a tariff-rate-change explanation for billing calculation defects, though it says nothing about non-tariff calculation bugs.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder statement that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative finding E-04 (tariff_change_log, 0 records) and adds no new information beyond corroboration.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) attributes the manual-read route shortfall to being three readers short since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for affected customers; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim offering a mechanism for the already-measured E-02 completion gap, not new measured data.

E-06 still shows SH-FIELD's non-authoritative claim that a reader staffing shortage since July causes late routes and resulting estimated bills — that stakeholder statement stands as given. It no longer plausibly explains the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills in E-01, since E-12 shows those bills come from AMI meters rejected at billing import, not from late manual-read routes.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly (E-07) shows monthly ticket counts of 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) 2026, quantifying that dispute volume roughly doubled from the Jun-Jul baseline into Aug-Sep. This confirms the magnitude of the surge referenced in the initial request but does not by itself identify any causal mechanism (read-source, calculation, staffing, or response-speed).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative document (service contract §4.2) establishing that the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this is the documentary basis for the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint, not new causal evidence about the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) lists 14 specific routes with per-route completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 0.88 completion figure in E-02. It identifies which routes are behind but does not itself join these routes to the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, so it narrows but does not close the quantification gap in U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 is a complete billing-db record of 320 distinct accounts billed from ESTIMATED reads in the latest cycle, each mapped to one of 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000/R-00). Its field set is limited to account_id and route — no import-status field — so while it supplies raw account-route data for the planned route/dispute join, it cannot serve as the import-validation-outcome proxy the plan assumed for testing ACTUAL-read dispute causes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which if true would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query; it does not itself contain any AMI read-event data or health status.

mdms-export shows that for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (matching E-01's ESTIMATED count exactly), the underlying meters are AMI, not manual field-read: 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read delivered before cutoff but rejected at billing import for high consumption, and only 56 (4.5%) had no AMI read received at all. This indicates the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment is driven by a billing import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads, not by the field manual-read route-completion shortfall (E-02) that the root problem attributes it to.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes disputes among the majority ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-01) that are not explained by estimate substitution?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any dispute-reduction automation beyond read-coverage remediation is justified; without this, over half the dispute volume has no evidenced fix.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Join DA-TICKET disputed ACTUAL-read bills against DA-RULES billing import rule changes and DA-BILL calculation/tariff fields by account and date to identify a distinct mechanism.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Ship diagnostic-only investigation of ACTUAL-read disputes; do not enable any bill-fixing automation for this segment until a cause is evidenced (SC-ROOT-CAUSE-SEGMENTATION).

U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.question: Does the field route-completion shortfall (E-02) quantitatively account for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-01), or only a fraction of them?
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.decision_impact: Sizes how much of the dispute surge route-completion remediation can actually resolve, versus other ESTIMATED-segment causes.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.resolution_path: Join DA-ROUTE shortfall accounts to DA-TICKET disputed ESTIMATED-read tickets by account id and date to quantify overlap.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.safe_placeholder: Treat the field-read-coverage mechanism as explaining only an unquantified part of the ESTIMATED segment until the join is run.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-QUANTIFIED-LIN.resolution: E-12 shows the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills trace to AMI read events (rejected-at-import or missing), not manual-read route-shortfall accounts; the field route-completion shortfall (E-02) therefore appears to account for essentially none of this segment, not a fraction of it.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-HEALTH.question: Does the AMI/MDMS export (currently DEGRADED, vendor access pending) show any degradation contributing to a subset of estimate substitutions, despite E-01 ruling out AMI/import failure as the primary driver?
U-MDMS-EXPORT-HEALTH.decision_impact: Determines whether AMI pipeline health needs separate remediation alongside field-read coverage.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution_path: Obtain vendor-provisioned mdms-export access (currently DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING) and re-run read_events_for_disputed_estimated once available.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-HEALTH.safe_placeholder: Continue using the crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly alternate path already adopted (recovery_decision seq 65) while mdms-export access is pending.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution: E-12 shows only 56/1240 (4.5%) ESTIMATED disputed bills had no AMI read received (possible export gap); the remaining 1184 were received and exported fine but rejected by a billing import rule, so MDMS export health is a minor, not primary, contributor.

U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.question: Is the reader staffing shortage since July (SH-FIELD claim, E-06) the actual cause of the route-completion shortfall, given SH-FIELD's incentive toward headcount increase and noted attribution bias?
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.decision_impact: Affects whether route-completion remediation should target staffing versus other operational causes.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.resolution_path: Request ORG-FIELD staffing/headcount records independent of SH-FIELD's interview claim to verify the reader-shortage mechanism.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.safe_placeholder: Treat staffing shortage as an unverified contributing hypothesis (E-06), not a confirmed cause, when scoping remediation.

U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Are the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL data handoffs delivering complete, semantically valid reads into billing, or could delivery failures themselves be contributing to estimate substitution?
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If either handoff is failing, read-source conclusions drawn from DA-BILL/DA-MDMS joins would be unreliable until corrected.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Verify delivery_status and semantic_validity of H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL against billing-db import logs for the Aug-Sep window.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat read-source mechanism conclusions as provisional until handoff delivery/semantic validity is confirmed; do not size remediation on them alone.

A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-TO-DISPUTE-L.statement: The route-completion shortfall measured in E-02 is assumed to translate into the ESTIMATED-read disputed bills counted in E-01, although no record directly joins shortfall accounts to specific disputed tickets.

A-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-CAUSE.statement: The route-completion shortfall is assumed to be caused by a reader staffing shortage since July, per SH-FIELD's non-authoritative claim, which has not been independently verified and carries a noted stakeholder bias/incentive.
